Find the area $A$ bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x=t,\,y=t\operatorname{sin}⁡t
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [\pi ,2\pi ].$ Do not round the answer.

$A=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t) \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a negative number since $\operatorname{sin}⁡t\le 0$ for all $t\in [\pi ,2\pi ]$ and $t\ge 0.$

To solve the above integral, we use integration by parts. We set

$$
\begin{aligned}u=t & ⇒ & {u}^{′}=1 \\ {v}^{′}=\operatorname{sin}⁡t & ⇒ & v=-\operatorname{cos}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t & =-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{\pi }^{2\pi }+{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\cdot 1\,\text{d}t \\  & =-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{\pi }^{2\pi }+{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }t\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\text{d}t| \\  & =|\,-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{\pi }^{2\pi }+{\int }_{\pi }^{2\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,\text{d}t\,| \\  & =|\,-t\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,{|}_{\pi }^{2\pi }+\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,{|}_{\pi }^{2\pi }\,| \\  & =|\,-(2\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡2\pi -\pi \operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )+(\operatorname{sin}⁡2\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi )\,| \\  & =|\,-(2\pi (1)-\pi (-1))\,| \\  & =3\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
